findings.title: Journal search with an apostrophe crashes the server (SQL built by string interpolation)
findings.steps: Open /journal and type it's in the search box (or open /journal?q=it's directly).
findings.expected: Entries matching it's are listed, or 'No entries match'.
findings.actual: The API returns 500 Internal Server Error and the page shows 'Could not load the journal.' The search term goes straight into the SQL (f"... LIKE '%{term}%'"), so a quote breaks the query. Input like x' OR 1=1 OR ' gets injected and returns every entry, and % or _ match everything.
findings.evidence: curl -G --data-urlencode "q=it's" /api/journal -> 'Internal Server Error' 500. In the browser, typing it's showed 'Could not load the journal.' Searching for % listed '4 entries match' (all of them).

findings.title: Journal load errors have no retry button
findings.where: /journal page and the Journal section of /plants/:id
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal fail (e.g. 502 with an HTML body), then open /journal or open a plant from the plants list.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that loads the data again once the server is back.
findings.actual: Only the text 'Could not load the journal.' is shown, with no way to retry except reloading the page or changing the search. On the plant page the only button in the Journal section is 'Add entry'.
findings.evidence: Journal section text: 'Entries, newest first / Could not load the journal.'; buttons in the section: ['Add entry'].

findings.title: Adding an entry spins forever when the server does not answer; no timeout
findings.where: /plants/:id New entry form (POST /api/journal); same for edit (PUT) and delete
findings.steps: Make POST /api/journal hang. Type an entry and click 'Add entry'. Wait 15 s.
findings.expected: The request times out after 10 s with a visible error, the button is enabled again and the text is kept.
findings.actual: The button still says 'Saving…' and stays disabled after 15 s. The API client has no timeout. When the stalled request finally got through, it created the entry anyway, so a user who reloads and tries again ends up with a duplicate entry (POST has no idempotency key).
findings.evidence: Form text after 15 s: 'Saving…'. After the route was released, the server had a new 'Hang test' entry.

findings.title: After a successful edit, a failed list refresh wipes out the whole journal list
findings.steps: Open a plant and click Edit on an entry. Make GET /api/journal?plant_id=... fail, then save the edit.
findings.expected: The saved entry is shown with its new text (from the PUT response), with at most a notice that the list could not be refreshed.
findings.actual: The PUT succeeds but the list disappears and only 'Could not load the journal.' is shown, with no retry. The 'saved' entry from the PUT response is ignored, because onEntrySaved only calls refreshJournal(), which clears the data when it fails.
findings.evidence: After saving, the .journal-list element was gone and the section showed 'Could not load the journal.'. The API confirmed the edit had been saved.

findings.title: Over-large IDs cause a 500 instead of a 4xx
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite integer overflow). /api/plants/{id} already behaves the same way, but the new endpoints also have no upper bound on IDs.
findings.evidence: All four requests returned 'Internal Server Error 500'.

findings.title: The browser limits the entry to 500 UTF-16 code units, so emoji text is capped at about 250 characters
findings.steps: Paste 260 emoji (🌱) into the entry textarea.
findings.expected: Up to 500 characters are accepted (the server counts code points and would accept 500 emoji).
findings.actual: The textarea's maxlength=500 cuts the text to 250 emoji and the counter says '0 characters left'.
findings.evidence: The textarea held 250 code points and the hint read '0 characters left'.
